introduction: On this seventh Sunday of Easter, between the Ascension and Pentecost, we listen to the prayer of Jesus for his disciples at the Last Supper: that the Father keep them, make them one, and consecrate them in the truth. In the first reading, the apostles choose Matthias to take the place of Judas. Like the first disciples gathered in prayer, let us ask the Father to send us the Holy Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus prayed for his disciples, and he prays for us. Let us join our prayers to his.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be one, as the Father and the Son are one, and consecrated in the truth. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are chosen for ministry and service in the Church: that they may be faithful witnesses of the Resurrection. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians who are hated or persecuted because of their faith: that the Father may keep them from the evil one. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are preparing for Confirmation: that they may be open to the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live in God's love, and prepare our hearts for the coming of the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Holy Father, your Son prayed that we might be one and kept from evil. Hear his prayer and ours, and send us the Holy Spirit to make us holy in the truth. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Keep them in your name
reflection.body:
In the days between the Ascension and Pentecost, the Church does what the first disciples did: she waits and prays. Today's Gospel lets us listen to Jesus himself praying for his disciples on the night before he died.

He knows he is about to leave them, and that they will stay behind in a hard world. So he prays: "Holy Father, keep them through your name which you have given me, that they may be one, even as we are." He does not ask the Father to take them out of the world: "I pray not that you would take them from the world, but that you would keep them from the evil one."

Then he asks the Father to make them holy: "Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth." And he sends them out just as he was sent: "As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world."

In the first reading, the community in Jerusalem gathers, about one hundred and twenty people. Peter explains that someone must take the place of Judas and become "a witness with us of his resurrection." They pray and choose Matthias. Even in that small and wounded community, the mission continues.

John's letter tells us how God remains with us now that Jesus has ascended: "If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us." And again: "God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him."

It is a great comfort to know that Jesus prays for us, by name, before the Father. This week, pray with him for the unity of Christians and for those who suffer for their faith. And ask, each day until Pentecost: Come, Holy Spirit.
